Proposition
[The Riemannian Volume Form]

↗ def:volume-form-pointwise ↗ prop:volume-form-smooth ↗ prop:volume-form-value-one ↗ prop:volume-form-uniqueness ↗ prop:volume-form-determinant ↗ prop:volume-form-coframe ↗ def:wedge-covectors ↗ prop:volume-form-coordinate-formula

1. ch2:2.41

On an oriented Riemannian $n$-manifold, with or without boundary, there is a unique smooth $n$-form $dV_g$ characterized equivalently by:

  1. $dV_g=e^1\wedge \cdots \wedge e^n$ for every local oriented orthonormal coframe;

  2. $dV_g(E_1,\ldots ,E_n)=1$ for every local oriented orthonormal frame;

  3. $dV_g=\sqrt{\det (g_{ij})}\, dx^1\wedge \cdots \wedge dx^n$ in every oriented coordinate chart.

Proof

↗ def:volume-form-pointwise ↗ prop:volume-form-smooth ↗ prop:volume-form-uniqueness ↗ prop:volume-form-coframe ↗ prop:volume-form-value-one ↗ prop:volume-form-coordinate-formula \sketch Definition 12 and Proposition 12 give a smooth form; Proposition 12 gives uniqueness from (b). Propositions 12, 12, and 12 establish (a)–(c), and each condition determines the same form by evaluation on an oriented orthonormal frame.

□

For a compactly supported continuous real-valued function $f$ on an oriented Riemannian manifold, define \[ \int _M f\, dV_g:=\int _M f dV_g, \qquad \operatorname {Vol}(M)=\int _MdV_g \] when $M$ is compact. The same definitions apply to a regular domain with its induced metric. If $M$ is compact, oriented, and without boundary, $dV_g$ is not exact because its integral is positive while exact forms integrate to zero. Properties (a) and (c) of Proposition 12 are independent of the wedge convention; the determinant convention makes (b) equal to $1$, while the Alt convention gives $1/n!$.
